A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Code2Logic/GameQA study. Their main text, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated case studies and expanded game documentation.

before.justification: v1 reports original human and model evaluations, SFT/GRPO training results, scaling experiments, and qualitative analyses in Tables 3–9 and Appendices B–D.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds Gemini evaluations and further empirical error analyses, including Appendix B.2 and Figure 8.

M1.justification: The game-code construction, QA-template design, and data-engine pipeline remain unchanged, as do augmentation, filtering, and SFT/GRPO procedures. Additional inference and game-specific documentation does not establish a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 30 GameQA games, 158 tasks, seven general benchmarks, and auxiliary training datasets. The expanded game catalog adds documentation rather than coverage. The 30K-to-140K prose correction agrees with dataset counts already present in v1 Table 2.

E2.justification: Gemini-2.5-Pro joins the GameQA comparisons in Tables 3 and 6 and the general-benchmark comparison in Table 4. Existing model and training-data comparators remain represented.

E3.justification: Appendix C.2 revises the human baseline from 20 random questions per game to 623 stratified questions, and the random baseline from guessing both answer types to expected multiple-choice scores with zero fill-in-the-blank credit. Section 4.5 reattributes the 790-case analysis from Qwen2.5-VL-7B to InternVL2.5-8B. These are reported setting revisions; the PDFs do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Appendix B.2 adds a before/after-GRPO breakdown of visual, textual, and combined errors, plus two text-reasoning improvement examples. Appendix I retains the four original GPT-4o cases and adds nine more. These extend existing diagnostic questions; the game-diversity and data-quantity analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain averaging over the three best validation-selected checkpoints among ten saved checkpoints for secondary experiments. Neither adds independent-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new error percentages are descriptive results.

E6.justification: New Gemini results lead Table 3 at 58.95% in-domain and 67.60% out-of-domain. Table 4 fills previously missing GPT-4o and Claude MMBench entries with 86.0 and 78.5. Figure 8 adds error-composition results. The introduction corrects Qwen's unseen-game gain from 3.83 to 3.42 percentage points, matching the unchanged Table 3; existing trained-model scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Neither version develops theoretical results or proofs. The retained mathematical reasoning in worked QA examples is unchanged; additional descriptive game rules and empirical error categories do not introduce a theoretical development.

C1.justification: v2 removes the claim that all evaluated models score below 50% and shifts the abstract, introduction, and conclusion toward controllable difficulty gradation. The central claims of game-code-based synthesis and cross-benchmark generalization remain intact.

C2.justification: New selection criteria in Appendix E.2 clarify applicability to games that are readily implementable and solvable from static images. Appendix I expands interpretations of failures, including card-pile orientation, missed snake collisions, and visual-perception bottlenecks. Appendix A's SFT and single-turn limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands reproducibility documentation: inference temperature 0.2 and the inference prompt, human-testing materials and participant conditions, game-selection criteria, and a catalog covering all 30 games with mechanics and difficulty parameters. The abstract also states that models are available alongside code and data. These are principally additional disclosures.

R1.justification: v2 adds Shao et al. (2024), DeepSeekMath, as the reference for GRPO. Section 5, Table 1, and the substantive positioning against previous dataset-construction and game-based work otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most retained prose remain intact. Local revisions clarify difficulty and evaluation descriptions, condense Appendix F.3's quality-assurance prose, and reorganize case studies and numbered game descriptions into separate appendices.

P2.justification: The appendices receive a substantial visual expansion: v1's two composite case figures become thirteen separately annotated case figures, accompanied by error charts, reasoning examples, human-test slides, and difficulty-image panels for additional games. v2 Figure 7 redisplays existing reasoning-change percentages with new examples. Tables 3, 4, and 6 also gain Gemini rows.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency through explicit inference and human-evaluation documentation and fuller game descriptions. Gemini comparisons and expanded diagnostics make benchmark performance easier to assess, while corrected dataset-size and generalization statements align with existing tables. These are useful refinements to an otherwise stable empirical contribution. The unexplained model reattribution in Section 4.5 leaves some uncertainty about that analysis's provenance.
